grants.award_text: Drug supply (sac-TMT) and/or total or partial study funding, negotiated per proposal; a line-item budget is required only if funding is requested
grants.eligibility: Open to investigators through Merck's MISP submission database; no rank, career-stage or citizenship cap is stated, but proposals will not be accepted from China, Hong Kong, Taiwan or Macau. A proposal must address at least one posted area of interest or it may be rejected without review. Applicants are told to consult their local Merck Research Medical Scientific Director (RMSD) before submitting, to check ClinicalTrials.gov so the study does not duplicate or compete with sac-TMT registration trials, and to supply letters of support for any third-party agent or funding. Less experienced investigators are encouraged to work with a mentor and include the mentor's CV and letter. Only MSD investigational agents named in the areas of interest are available for IIS use.
grants.notes: OPEN CALL WITH A HARD DATE: Merck is 'currently accepting proposals for the sac-TMT Investigator-Initiated Studies Program (IISP)' with proposals due to the IIS database by November 30, 2026 and decisions communicated in April 2027. sac-TMT is Merck's TROP2 antibody-drug conjugate, so this is the ADC-resistance and ADC-sequencing question in a sponsor-funded form. The breast areas of interest are (1) monotherapy or combination with pembrolizumab in early disease and (2) monotherapy in metastatic breast cancer in approved biomarker-selected populations, e.g. BRCA, in all breast cancer subtypes; the clinical translational areas are mechanisms of response and resistance to sac-TMT alone or with pembrolizumab, mechanisms to overcome that resistance, and effects on the tumor microenvironment, all in tissue samples, plus preclinical in-vitro and PDX work. Longitudinal sampling and neoadjuvant designs are 'strongly encouraged', which suits a HER2-heterogeneity or ctDNA-tracked correlative design layered on a sac-TMT study. THE TRAPS: safety-only primary endpoints are out of scope; phase I studies, biomarker identification or validation as the primary aim, technology development, vaccines, cell therapy, pediatric and microbiome studies are discouraged; a proposal that duplicates or competes with a sac-TMT registration trial will not be supported; translational primary endpoints must use samples from patients treated with MSD or standard-of-care agents per the AoIs, be adequately powered, and commit to data sharing per Merck's Data Tiers; the program asks how the study will support diversity in enrollment. Review is described as highly competitive on merit, strategic fit and feasibility. WHAT TO DO: consult the Merck RMSD for the region first, then submit the form, a CV dated within two years and, if funding is requested, the budget template through the IIS database before November 30, 2026. The compound list on the MISP solid-tumor page is watched daily; this per-compound page is server-rendered and watched too.

grants.notes: BREAST-SPECIFIC REAL-WORLD DATA AT SCALE, AND THE CHEAPEST ROUTE TO A PUBLISHABLE DATASET IN THIS SET. FLEX is a large prospective observational study linking full genome expression profiling, including MammaPrint and BluePrint, with complete clinical data in early-stage breast cancer, explicitly built to generate hypotheses for targeted investigator-initiated studies. Investigators at participating sites propose their own sub-studies to a central review committee; the programme reports 59 sub-study proposals submitted with 27 approved projects completed or underway, and fourteen investigator-initiated sub-study abstracts presented in 2025, so it demonstrably produces output. It suits an ER+ early-stage endocrine-resistance or genomic-signature question and needs no new accrual. THE GATING QUESTION IS SITE MEMBERSHIP, not eligibility: confirm whether the institution is among the participating sites and, if not, what joining involves. A CAUTION ON A CONFUSABLE NAME: the FLEX National PI is at Baylor University Medical Center in Dallas, which is a different institution from Baylor College of Medicine in Houston, so access does not follow from the name.

grants.notes: The Roderick D. MacDonald Research Fund is a Baylor St. Luke's Medical Center endowment, administered through BCM's Office of Research IT page, that awards up to $50,000 for one year with five review deadlines annually (2026: Jan 7, Mar 9, May 7, Aug 7, Nov 9). It is open to BSLMC professional staff and associated investigators, and explicitly to clinicians from other institutions whose collaborative project involves St. Luke's staff and is conducted at BSLMC or an affiliate, so a BCM breast medical oncologist practicing at Baylor St. Luke's is a natural applicant. For the PI it is the quickest local source of seed money for a ctDNA/MRD or EHR pilot, a biomarker sub-study nested in an existing trial, or start-up costs for an investigator-initiated trial. The trap is sequencing: the committee will not consider a proposal until a St. Luke's-accepted IRB (Baylor, BRANY, UT or CHI) has already approved the protocol, so the IRB submission must precede the fund application by months, and the budget cannot carry indirects, travel, publication costs or more than $10,000 in salary. The committee gives highest priority to work with clinical application to the quality or safety of care for hospitalized BSLMC patients, so an outpatient breast biomarker project should articulate a concrete care-delivery payoff at St. Luke's. Applications are delivered on paper to the committee chair and the BSLMC Office of Research (Neurosensory Building, 3rd floor). Next step: obtain IRB approval for the pilot protocol now and target the November 9, 2026 deadline; the committee normally meets within three weeks of each deadline.

grants.notes: The Chao Physician-Scientist Award is a BCM intramural award, funded by the Ting Tsung and Wei Fong Chao Foundation and run through the ICTR/Office of Research awards portal, giving up to two physicians $100,000 for one year as interim support while they secure a K08 or K23. It is distinct from the held BCM Interim Funding Program, which bridges lapsed extramural support; this one funds the pre-K gap and explicitly asks for prior K critiques and responses. For the PI, an MD-only breast oncologist with clinical duties at BCM, the eligibility gate (physician, primary full-time BCM appointment) is met, and any research angle qualifies, so a ctDNA/MRD real-world data project or an ER+/HER2+ biomarker project could be the vehicle. The trap is the framing: the award is written for "young investigators beginning their independent research careers" who are actively pursuing a K08/K23, so a year-7+ assistant professor who is not on a K trajectory will not read as the intended candidate, and reviewers will expect a concrete K23 submission plan (or a scored resubmission) in the application. The application page returned 404 on 2026-09-10 and no current deadline is posted; the last documented deadline was 2024-05-06 and FY26 awards were announced in July 2025, so the cycle appears to close each spring. Next step for the PI: email awards@bcm.edu or ICTR@bcm.edu to confirm the FY28 timeline and whether faculty beyond five years of appointment are considered, and decide whether a K23 is genuinely on the roadmap before investing in this application.
grants.evidence: ICTR index page (orit.research.bcm.edu/ictr/index.html) lists a link titled "Chao Physician-Scientist Award" pointing to orit.research.bcm.edu/R5T80IF3WH2/ChaoAward/Default.aspx, which returned HTTP 404, as did .../ChaoAward/Index (establishes the program is listed by ICTR but the application page is currently down). A second cached snippet: deadline "May 6, 2024 at 5:00 PM" and "made possible through a generous gift from the Ting Tsung and Wei Fong Chao Foundation" (establishes past cycle timing and funder). grants.indirects: Not allowed: the general guidelines state the Foundation does not support indirect costs or overhead allocated to projects.

grants.eligibility: Applicants are institutions, not individuals: applications from an individual researcher are not considered, and each medical research institution may submit exactly one application per grant cycle regardless of open grants or number of affiliated entities, approved by the Provost or Vice President for Research, with internal competition preferred. Eligible organizations are IRS 501(c)(3) public charities or public universities under section 170(c), and the Foundation currently refuses applications or pre-requests from organizations that have received no Kleberg funding in the past ten years; BCM clears that bar with awards in 2017, 2021, 2023, 2024 and 2025. Priority goes to institutions with a long-standing Foundation relationship, preferably in Texas. No degree, rank, track, career-stage, or clinical-duty restriction is placed on the investigator.
grants.notes: The Kleberg Foundation Medical Research Grant is a Texas-priority private mechanism that funds highly innovative basic and applied biomedical research at roughly $1.5M over three years, with two cycles a year closing 31 March and 30 September. It matters to the PI because BCM is an established Kleberg grantee (awards in 2017, 2021, 2023, 2024 and 2025), Rice received $1.56M in 2025 for a breast cancer diagnostic, and cancer biomarker and immunotherapy projects were funded in the same cycle, so translational work on HER2 heterogeneity, endocrine resistance or ctDNA biomarkers is within the Foundation's range. The trap is that this is not something the PI can apply to directly: the Foundation refuses applications from individual researchers, BCM gets one slot per cycle chosen by internal competition and signed by the Provost or VP Research, and no indirect costs are paid, so the department must absorb overhead. The 30 September 2026 fall deadline is open on the Foundation side, but BCM's internal selection for that cycle has almost certainly closed. The PI should ask the BCM Office of Research or the limited-submissions coordinator when the spring 2027 internal call opens (Foundation window 1 February to 31 March 2027) and prepare a one-page concept pitched as groundbreaking biology rather than incremental trial work, since the Foundation's language favors top-tier innovation and its awards skew toward senior labs. Note also that the finder's claim about a Pre-Request route for unfunded institutions is wrong on the current page, which states such organizations are not accepted at all.

grants.indirects: None allowed: "Funds can be applied to direct costs only (no institution overhead or indirect costs)." PI salary capped at 10% of the award; no travel, publication fees, or student support; equipment capped at $10,000.

grants.eligibility: The applicant must hold an MD or MD/PhD (or equivalent) and a faculty position at an accredited academic medical center, university or research institution in the US, US territories or Canada, and must conduct the majority of the research there. Each project has a single PI who is responsible for oversight and financial management. No career-stage, age, years-since-training, rank, or tenure-track requirement is stated, and clinical duties are not restricted. The project must be a therapeutic development program (small molecule, biologic, or other therapeutic modality) addressing an unmet medical need with a strong IP or protection strategy; diagnostics or devices qualify only as part of a therapeutic project.
grants.notes: The Harrington Scholar-Innovator Award is a national, annual physician-scientist drug-development award from the Harrington Discovery Institute at University Hospitals (Cleveland): a two-year $100,000 direct-cost grant, a chance to compete for up to $300,000 in acceleration funds and up to about $2MM in investment, and a dedicated drug-development team and project manager. It is one of the few mechanisms that requires an MD (or MD/PhD) rather than a PhD, has no career-stage cap, and does not restrict clinical duties, so the PI clears every eligibility line. The trap is scope: the program funds therapeutic development of a specific small molecule, biologic, or other modality with a defensible IP position, and diagnostics or devices only when embedded in such a project. The PI's leading angles (EHR/ctDNA real-world data, investigator-initiated trials, biomarker discovery) do not qualify, and only a novel agent for HER2-heterogeneous or endocrine-resistant disease with institutional IP would. The award also allows no indirect costs and caps PI salary at 10%, which BCM sponsored programs will need to accept. The 2026 cycle closed 2026-06-22 and the 2027 class is announced March 2027; dates for the next call have not been posted, but the pattern is a mid-April opening and a late-June deadline. The PI should log this as a spring-2027 target only if a proprietary therapeutic candidate exists, and otherwise treat it as a low-priority mechanism.

BCM's giving page cites 'nearly $850,000' to Baylor breast cancer research over close to two decades, including one $40,000 imaging-equipment gift.

grants.eligibility: No eligibility criteria, RFA, or application process are published anywhere on nobcf.org. The foundation directs its annual proceeds to three standing beneficiaries: the Lester and Sue Smith Breast Center at BCM (currently a named basic-science lab working on aging, metastasis, treatment resistance and endocrine resistance in ER+ disease), MD Anderson (a breast cancer prevention vaccine program), and Houston Methodist's Department of Nanomedicine. Support is relationship-mediated through each institution's leadership and development office, not competitive. A BCM assistant professor with clinical duties is not excluded by any stated rule, but would need the Smith Breast Center director and BCM Foundation Relations to put a project forward.
grants.notes: The Nancy Owens Breast Cancer Foundation is an all-volunteer Houston nonprofit (founded after its namesake's death in 2001) that raises money through an annual October luncheon and a Fashion for the Cure event and hands the proceeds to three fixed beneficiaries: the Smith Breast Center at BCM, MD Anderson, and Houston Methodist's nanomedicine department. There is no grant program: nobcf.org has no RFA, no application, no deadline, and no eligibility text, and the foundation's own archive shows the money arriving as luncheon-day checks (2023: $120,000 split three ways; 2022: $165,000). The BCM share has historically gone to one established basic-science lab whose current project is described as work on endocrine resistance in ER+ breast cancer, which is thematically close to the PI's third angle but is already spoken for. The finder's claim that the foundation 'plays a pivotal role in securing federal and state funding' could not be found on any nobcf.org page or the BCM giving page and should be discarded. The trap is treating this as something to apply to; it is a donor relationship owned by the Smith Breast Center director and BCM Office of Development, and any support for the PI would be a directed gift of roughly $40,000 negotiated through them. What the PI should do: ask the Smith Breast Center leadership whether the foundation's BCM allocation is reviewed annually and whether a clinical or real-world-data project could be presented as a second beneficiary before the October 16, 2026 25th-anniversary luncheon, when the year's gifts are typically presented. Fit is modest because the award is small, non-competitive, and currently directed elsewhere.

The only formal RFA the foundation ever posted was its first, in 2018 ("offering our first request for applications"), and that page's PDFs are the sole written criteria; nothing newer exists on the site. Funded investigators to date sit at MD Anderson, Dana-Farber, Vanderbilt, Duke, Ohio State and the University of Delaware, spanning laboratory, translational and social-science work, so there is no institutional, degree or career-stage restriction in evidence. A BCM assistant professor with clinical duties would face no stated barrier; the practical gate is whether the project is squarely about inflammatory breast cancer.
grants.notes: The IBC Network Foundation is a Sealy, Texas patient-founded charity whose sole research purpose is inflammatory breast cancer; its funding page is a ledger of roughly $2.0M released from 2012 through 2026, not an application guide. There is no open call: the foundation issued one formal RFA in 2018 and has since funded by invitation and direct negotiation, with awards documented at $1,500 to $150,000 and a 2026 research grant of $50,000. For the PI this is a pilot-scale, non-competitive-calendar source that fits only if a project is framed around IBC itself, where HER2-positive disease is over-represented and the world's largest IBC clinic sits at MD Anderson across the Texas Medical Center. A HER2-heterogeneity, ADC-response or ctDNA/real-world outcomes sub-study restricted to IBC patients is the natural pitch; a generic ER+/HER2+ proposal will not be funded. The trap is treating the 2018 RFA page as a live mechanism, or assuming indirects are paid. Next step: send a one-page concept to hello@theibcnetwork.org, ideally co-developed with an MD Anderson IBC collaborator, and ask what the foundation is funding in the current year.

grants.notes: The Anna Fuller Fund is a perpetual private foundation administered by Wells Fargo Philanthropic Services that makes 5-8 cancer research or education grants a year, averaging $75,000-$150,000 each, to 501(c)(3) organizations for a specific cancer research project. For the PI it is a pilot-scale, no-strings source: there is no degree, career-stage, track, or clinical-duty gate, no cancer-type restriction, and a 2025 award of $150,000 went to a breast cancer research project at Dana-Farber, so a ctDNA/EHR registry study or an ER+/HER2+ biomarker project fits the stated purpose. The trap is that the applicant is the institution, not the PI: the online CyberGrants form is submitted in BCM's name, so the PI must route the request through BCM Foundation Relations and sponsored programs early rather than filing it personally, and should ask Wells Fargo grant administration whether indirect costs are allowable since the page is silent. Applications are accepted year-round but only those in by July 31 are reviewed at the year-end meeting, with decisions communicated by January; the 2026 cycle has closed, so the PI should target the July 31, 2027 deadline and confirm the date on the page in spring 2027. Periodic progress and final reports may be required. Fit is moderate: the award is small relative to a federal grant but well matched to generating preliminary data.

grants.eligibility: Open to 'external independent investigators, organizations, and institutions (academic, private, or governmental)' who will act as the regulatory sponsor of the study. Jazz states it 'only supports study proposals that have a legitimate scientific purpose' and that it does not support studies as a reward for using, purchasing, recommending or prescribing Jazz products. Requests go through the iEnvision online portal (program code ISR) after account registration; submission does not guarantee approval.
grants.notes: Jazz Pharmaceuticals' Investigator Sponsored Trials (IST) programme is a rolling industry portal, structurally identical to the held AstraZeneca, Daiichi Sankyo, Merck and Genentech records: the investigator's institution sponsors the study and Jazz may supply study drug, funding, or both, with amounts negotiated per proposal. It matters to the PI because Jazz owns zanidatamab (Ziihera), a HER2 bispecific already FDA-approved in biliary tract and first-line HER2+ gastroesophageal cancer and now in phase 3 (EmpowHER-BC-303, post-T-DXd metastatic HER2+ breast cancer) and phase 2 neoadjuvant breast trials, plus combination programmes with HER2 TKIs; that makes it the most direct industry route for an investigator-initiated study in HER2 heterogeneity, triple-positive disease or post-ADC resistance not already covered by the held portals. The trap is that the public page publishes neither areas of research interest nor amounts nor review timelines; those sit behind the iEnvision portal login (jazz.envisionpharma.com, pgm=ISR), and the sponsor's breast-cancer interest cannot be confirmed from the public page. The PI should register a portal account, read the posted areas of interest, and email researchgrant@jazzpharma.com with a one-paragraph concept before drafting a full proposal. Because the investigator (or BCM) must act as regulatory sponsor, an IND or IND-exemption path and BCM's clinical research office should be lined up first. The record is 'needs-check' only because the portal-gated areas of interest have not been read, not because of any stated eligibility barrier.

grants.eligibility: The public page states only that NeoGenomics welcomes collaboration requests for all types of investigator-initiated studies that would benefit from its testing modalities and technology. No career-stage, degree, rank, track or institutional gate is stated, and there is no stated exclusion of investigators with clinical duties. The investigator sponsors the study and NeoGenomics contributes testing; terms are negotiated case by case after a request through the Smartsheet contact form. There is no published application, review committee, or budget.
grants.notes: NeoGenomics publishes a one-line open invitation for investigator-initiated study collaborations that would benefit from its testing modalities, reached through a Smartsheet contact form on the providers support-resources page; there is no formal program, deadline, review committee or published budget. The relevant asset for this profile is RaDaR ST, a tumor-informed ctDNA MRD assay built from whole-exome data of the tumor, which NeoGenomics markets to biopharma for enriching trial populations and following treatment response and which cites the PENELOPE-B ER+/HER2-negative breast cancer ctDNA work on its pharma page. For the PI this is the cheapest realistic route to add serial MRD readouts to an EHR- or registry-anchored ER+/HER2+ cohort or to a small investigator-initiated trial without buying assays from a grant, and it complements rather than duplicates the held Exact Sciences (Oncotype DX) and Agendia (FLEX transcriptome) records, neither of which supplies ctDNA. The trap is treating this as funding: support is in kind, the terms, sample volumes, data-sharing and publication rights are negotiated case by case, and the website gives no indication of how many academic requests are accepted. A second trap is over-claiming the assay on the web pages: the NeoGenomics pages fetched today do not state the number of variants tracked or a formal breast-cancer validation, so any proposal should cite the peer-reviewed RaDaR literature rather than the vendor site. Next step is a short concept note (cohort, timepoints, sample counts, endpoints, what NeoGenomics would contribute) submitted through the form, in parallel with a Duncan CC biospecimen and IRB plan so the request is concrete; pair it with a cash mechanism (for example a Duncan pilot or DOD BCRP) that pays for coordinators and analysis.

grants.sponsor_full: American Association for Cancer Research — Project GENIE (Genomics Evidence Neoplasia Information Exchange) and the GENIE Biopharma Collaborative (BPC)
grants.program: GENIE public registry and GENIE BPC clinico-genomic data access
grants.award_text: No funding. Deliverable is data access: the GENIE public registry (20.0-public, July 2026, >289,000 samples from >242,000 patients) plus six publicly released BPC clinico-genomic cohorts (NSCLC 2.0, CRC 2.0, BRCA 1.0, PANC 1.0, Prostate 1.0, Bladder 1.0).
grants.typical_month: Registry releases every January and July; access is continuous
flags: not-funding
data-resource
terms-of-access-unverified
grants.eligibility: Any researcher may use the data; there is no competitive review, no institutional consortium membership requirement and no fee stated. The page says users must create an account on cBioPortal or Synapse and agree to the terms of access; the terms themselves are on the Synapse pages, which could not be rendered. Published work must cite the 2017 Cancer Discovery GENIE paper and carry the stated acknowledgment. The PI's rank, degree, track and clinical duties are irrelevant.
grants.notes: AACR Project GENIE is a publicly accessible pan-cancer clinico-genomic registry, not a grant: release 20.0-public (July 2026) holds more than 289,000 sequenced samples from more than 242,000 patients, updated each January and July, with 21.0-public expected January 2027. The Biopharma Collaborative layer adds deep longitudinal clinical curation, and six BPC cohorts are public today, including BRCA 1.0-public drawn from an early-onset breast cancer cohort. For the PI this is a zero-cost substrate for a computational/real-world-data paper (treatment sequencing, genomic correlates of endocrine resistance or HER2 heterogeneity) that can serve as preliminary data for funded mechanisms already in the database. Access needs only a cBioPortal or Synapse account and agreement to the terms of access; no institutional agreement or review is described on the page, though the terms themselves live on Synapse and were not readable here. The trap: the BPC breast cohort is early-onset and the registry is skewed to institutions doing targeted panel sequencing, so ER+/HER2+ subset sizes and receptor annotation should be confirmed in the data guide before an analysis is promised. Next step is to register, download the BRCA 1.0-public data guide and the genieBPC R package, and scope a subtype question that a mechanism such as a Komen, BCRF or NCI R21/R01 aim could build on.
grants.evidence: "AACR Project GENIE® 20.0-public was released in July 2026" and "more than 289,000 sequenced samples from more than 242,000 patients" (establish current release and scale); "updated twice annually (January and July)" and "AACR Project GENIE® 21.0-public (Expected January 2027)" (establish cadence, no deadline); "Users will need to create an account for either site and agree to the terms of access" (establish open access without competitive review); BPC "deeply clinically annotated nearly 8,000 patients with lung, colorectal, early-onset breast, pancreatic, prostate, and bladder cancers" and the public dataset list including "BRCA 1.0-public" (establish breast cohort availability); FAQ: "any work using GENIE data must include proper attribution" (publication condition).

grants.award_text: Not published. The page lists "Clinical studies / IITs", educational events, publication support and corporate giving as fundable request types but states no award amounts, budget ranges or caps; support (funding and, presumably, assay access) is negotiated case by case through the Versaic proposal portal.

grants.eligibility: US applicants must be a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization unless the request is for a CME/CEU-accredited program; international applicants must be a non-profit equivalent and apply via the Corporate Giving form. Requests must be submitted at least 60 days before the initiative's start date, and post-dated events are not considered. The page sets no restriction on disease area, degree, career stage, appointment track or clinical duties; the applicant of record is the institution, so a BCM assistant professor with clinical responsibilities can be the named investigator. Excluded categories include HCP travel, unstructured meetings without educational goals, advertising or marketing, equipment purchases and restricted grants.
grants.notes: The Hologic Grant Program is the company's single intake for medical-education grants, investigator-initiated trials, publication support and corporate giving, run through a Versaic proposal portal rather than a scientific competition. It matters to the PI because Hologic owns Biotheranostics and the Breast Cancer Index (BCI), the assay used to guide extended endocrine therapy in HR+ disease, which sits directly on the endocrine-resistance angle and could anchor a real-world-data or registry study of BCI-guided decisions, or a ctDNA/MRD correlative attached to a BCI cohort. The page confirms "Clinical studies / IITs" are in scope and that BCM, as a 501(c)(3), is an eligible applicant; it imposes no career-stage, degree, track or clinical-duty restriction. The trap is treating this as a funding announcement: no award sizes, review criteria or decision timelines are published, and the page warns that not every request is supported, so the proposal must make an explicit case that ties to a Hologic product line (BCI, or a diagnostic or imaging platform) and should be sized realistically for corporate IIT support. Requests must be filed at least 60 days before the intended start, and post-dated activities are refused. Next step: register an account at hologic.versaic.com, confirm with BCM's industry-contracts office how IIT budgets and indirects are handled for Hologic agreements, and open a parallel scientific conversation with Biotheranostics medical affairs before submitting so the portal request lands with a known reviewer.

grants.career_cap: Mid-career: faculty appointment at a SWOG member institution or 8-14 years of clinical research experience; active K/ACS/DOD career development awardees excluded
grants.eligibility: Mid-career investigators who hold a faculty appointment at a SWOG member institution, or who can show 8-14 years of clinical research experience (e.g., a leadership role on a protocol development team). The applicant must be a SWOG member at a SWOG member institution at the time of award, must have at least 25% protected time for clinical/translational research, and may not hold an active multi-year career development award (K-award, ACS, DOD). The proposed research must use SWOG resources (a project approved by a Disease Working Group or triage committee, pending or recently activated in SWOG, or using SWOG specimens, clinical data or imaging) and needs a letter from the relevant SWOG committee chair plus a letter from the institutional SWOG PI. International applicants from SWOG institutions are welcome; no degree or tenure-track restriction is stated.
grants.notes: The Hope Foundation's Career Engagement Award buys protected time for mid-career SWOG investigators: $100,000 over two years, paid as $50,000 per year of salary and fringe for the candidate only, with no indirects. It is the one Hope Foundation mechanism pitched above the early-career Coltman fellowship, and its research criteria explicitly include projects that use SWOG specimens, clinical data or imaging as well as concepts pending or recently activated in SWOG, which maps onto the PI's real-world-data, biomarker and investigator-initiated-trial angles. For a seventh-year assistant professor the eligibility language ("hold a faculty appointment at a SWOG member institution or demonstrate 8-14 years of experience in clinical research") reads as satisfied by the faculty appointment alone, but the RFA invites applicants unsure of their career stage to email jo@thehopefoundation.org, and the PI should do that before investing effort. Three traps: the PI must be a SWOG member at a SWOG member institution at the time of award, so Baylor's SWOG membership and the PI's individual membership need confirming first; anyone holding an active multi-year career development award (K, ACS, DOD) is ineligible; and the application needs a letter with a priority score from the SWOG Breast Committee chair and a letter from the institutional SWOG PI, which takes lead time. The 2026 form is closed and the programs index lists the award as "Coming Soon", so the 2027-03-15 date is projected from the stated annual March 15 cycle rather than posted. Next step: confirm SWOG membership status, line up a breast-committee-endorsed project, and watch the Foundation site in early 2027 for the form to reopen.

grants.career_cap: Early-career faculty appointment (Assistant Professor, Clinical Instructor, Lecturer) OR 0-7 years of clinical research experience; no active multi-year CDA (K, ACS, DOD)
grants.eligibility: The applicant must hold an early-career faculty appointment (Assistant Professor, Clinical Instructor, or Lecturer) at a SWOG member institution, or demonstrate 0-7 years of clinical research experience; the two clauses are joined by "or", so an assistant professor qualifies by rank. Applicants must be SWOG members at a SWOG member institution at the time of award (Baylor College of Medicine is listed as SWOG institution #11988), must commit at least 25% protected effort to clinical/translational research and to this project, and must name a Primary Mentor who is active in SWOG as a PI, committee chair/vice chair, or contributing member. Candidates holding an active multi-year career development award (K-award, ACS, DOD) are not eligible. The project must use SWOG resources (a committee-approved or activated SWOG project, or SWOG specimens/clinical data/imaging) and requires letters from the institutional SWOG PI and the relevant SWOG Disease Committee chair, the latter with a priority score. International applicants from SWOG institutions may apply.
grants.notes: The Coltman Fellowship is The Hope Foundation's two-year, $100,000 salary award that buys protected time for an early-career investigator at a SWOG member institution to develop a SWOG-associated clinical or translational project under a SWOG-active mentor, with travel to four consecutive SWOG Group Meetings paid on top. For the PI it is the cash-and-mentorship layer on the held SWOG Breast Committee concept route: an investigator-initiated breast concept worked through the Breast Committee, or a secondary analysis of SWOG breast trial specimens or clinical data (ctDNA, endocrine resistance, HER2 heterogeneity), is exactly the "must involve SWOG resources" requirement. The 2026 RFA defines eligibility as an early-career faculty appointment (Assistant Professor, Clinical Instructor, Lecturer) OR 0-7 years of clinical research experience, so eligibility rests on rank rather than years, and an assistant professor beyond year 7 still qualifies; the RFA invites an eligibility-check email to jo@thehopefoundation.org, which is worth sending before investing effort. The traps are structural: the PI must be a registered SWOG member (Baylor College of Medicine is SWOG institution #11988, so this is a membership step, not an institutional barrier), must not hold an active multi-year K, ACS or DOD career development award at the time of award, must commit 25% effort, and needs a Disease Committee chair letter with a priority score, which means the project has to be in the SWOG breast pipeline months before March. No indirect costs are paid and the budget is salary and fringe only. Applications are due March 15 annually; the 2026 cycle has passed, so the working target is 2027-03-15 (projected from the page, not yet posted). Next step: confirm SWOG membership status, identify a SWOG Breast Committee mentor, and get a concept or SWOG data-use request in front of the committee before the winter.

grants.award_text: In-kind statistical analysis support, not a cash award to the applicant: funded SWOG Statistics and Data Management Center analyst time for a database analysis using SWOG trial data alone or linked to registry (SEER) or claims (SEER-Medicare) data. The RFA states that all associated funds are paid directly to the SWOG Statistical Center; no dollar figure is published.
grants.indirects: Not applicable; funds go directly to the SWOG Statistical Center, nothing flows to the applicant's institution.

grants.eligibility: The RFA says any SWOG investigator eligible for NIH funding may submit; the program page lists the applicant type as SWOG Member Investigators, and SWOG membership is held at the institution level (member institution, NCORP member, or affiliate). There is no career-stage cap, no track requirement, and no restriction on clinical duties. Priority goes to investigators who are active in SWOG activities, and the project must be completable within one year with a manuscript expected within 90 days of analysis completion. Applicants may submit more than one scientifically distinct application.
grants.notes: The Hope Foundation's Secondary Data Analysis Program is a standing, rolling-submission mechanism that pairs a SWOG member investigator with the SWOG Statistics and Data Management Center to run a database analysis on completed SWOG trial data, alone or linked to SEER or SEER-Medicare claims. It is not a cash grant: the RFA states all associated funds are paid directly to the SWOG Statistical Center, so the PI receives analyst time and data access rather than budget. That makes it a direct match for the PI's first-priority angle of real-world and registry-linked outcomes work, and it is a low-cost route to a first-author cooperative-group paper drawing on SWOG breast trials with ER+ and HER2+ populations. The application is deliberately light (one-page cover letter, one-page analysis plan specifying outcomes, predictors and any claims codes, NIH-style biosketch, other support), and more than one distinct project may be submitted. The trap is membership: the applicant type is SWOG Member Investigators and membership is institutional, so the PI should confirm that BCM is an active SWOG member site and that the PI is registered, then engage the SWOG Breast Committee so the concept reads as aligned with the Group's portfolio, which reviewers score explicitly. A second caution is that the RFA is dated February 2022 even though it was re-uploaded in March 2026, and the number of projects per year is limited and funding-contingent, so the PI should email the program contact to confirm capacity before investing effort. Nothing in this program overlaps the held Impact Award or SEED Fund records; the SEED Fund also permits secondary data analysis but is a separate annual cash award.

grants.career_cap: No PI or co-PI role on a clinical trial or NIH R-level grant within the past 10 years; must have completed fellowship/postdoc training
grants.eligibility: Medical, surgical, gynecologic or radiation oncologists, or PhD-prepared researchers, who have completed fellowship or postdoc training. The applicant must not have been a principal investigator or co-principal investigator on a clinical trial or an NIH R-level grant within the past 10 years. Prior NRG Oncology experience or a commitment to future NRG involvement is required, along with institutional support for a minimum 10% FTE commitment and acceptance of a 10% indirect-cost cap. No degree, faculty-track or clinical-duty restriction is stated; the 2025 call named breast cancer research among the specific opportunities.
grants.notes: A two-year, $50,000 ($25,000/yr) mentored fellowship run by NRG Oncology's NCORP research base that pairs an early-stage investigator with a senior NRG mentor to carry a health-care-access concept through NRG protocol development, with the fellow expected to serve as PI of the resulting trial. It is distinct from the held NRG Early Career Mentored Fellowship (April 30 cycle, unfunded) and from generic concept submission: this one carries money, a named funder slot (BCRF funded the 2026 breast fellow), and mandatory HCA Committee engagement, so it is the cleanest conversion of the PI's health-equity angle into cooperative-group trial leadership. The trap is the career cap: anyone who has been PI or co-PI on any clinical trial or NIH R-level grant in the past 10 years is ineligible, which an investigator-initiated-trial record could trigger; the PI should confirm standing before drafting. The 10% indirect cap and 10% FTE commitment need BCM and division sign-off, and the fellow must attend every summer and winter NRG meeting for two years. Applications are accepted yearly in the fall; the 2026-27 call closed September 19, 2025 and the 2022 call also closed September 19, so the 2027-28 call is likely imminent but was not posted on the program page or news feed as of 2026-09-10. Next step: watch the program page for the 2026 announcement PDF, line up an NRG breast-committee mentor, and prepare a one-page access-focused concept (for example ctDNA/MRD-guided surveillance access or ADC delivery in rural or safety-net populations) that also serves the PI's real-world-data angle. Prior calls routed applications to Fellowships@NRGOncology.org.

grants.eligibility: The page states only that data and specimens "are available to approved investigators by completing an I-SPY Concept Proposal" and that the DAPC "reviews all proposals to ensure scientific rigor, feasibility, and alignment with QLHC's mission." No degree, career-stage, track, institutional-membership, or clinical-duty requirement is published, and the page does not say whether applicants must be at an I-SPY site. grants.notes: Quantum Discovery is Quantum Leap Healthcare Collaborative's data-access programme for the I-SPY platform: DAPC-approved investigators who file an I-SPY Concept Proposal get structured access to 12+ years of neoadjuvant trial data and 500,000+ annotated biospecimens, including longitudinal ctDNA, serial MRI, and WGS/WES/RNA-seq. It is a resource, not a grant; no money is attached and any cost-recovery terms are unpublished. For the PI it is a fast route to test HER2-heterogeneity, endocrine-resistance, or ctDNA/MRD hypotheses on a deep multi-modal breast cohort without opening a trial, and it pairs naturally with a computational or biomarker application to a funder that wants existing data in hand. A second trap is the finder's claim that the Endocrine Optimization Pilot is "directly on-topic": that arm is HR+/HER2-negative, so the triple-positive angle depends on I-SPY 2's HR+/HER2+ subgroups instead. Next step: contact QLHC via contact-us to obtain the concept-proposal template, DAPC review timeline, and data-use/cost terms, then scope a concept around ctDNA dynamics or HER2 heterogeneity in HR+/HER2+ patients.

grants.eligibility: Applicants must hold an MD, PhD, DO, PharmD or equivalent doctoral degree, be US citizens, nationals or permanent residents, and be employed by a domestic nonprofit or government entity. New applicants must have total qualifying educational debt equal to or exceeding 20 percent of institutional annual base salary at award (waived for renewals) and must commit to an average of at least 20 hours per week of qualified clinical research during each quarterly service period; NIH research funding is not required. Qualified research is patient-oriented research with human subjects, epidemiologic, behavioral, outcomes or health-services research, which covers EHR, ctDNA/MRD and registry work. Ineligible are those with a federal judgment lien, an unresolved health-professional service obligation, federal employment over 20 hours per week, any research support or salary from a for-profit organization, or current IRTA/CRTA awards; only one LRP application per fiscal year is allowed.
grants.notes: The NIH Extramural Loan Repayment Program for Clinical Researchers (LRP-CR, L30) repays up to $50,000 per year of qualified educational debt for doctoral-level investigators who commit to at least 20 hours per week of clinical research at a domestic nonprofit or government employer. The FY2027 notice NOT-OD-26-081 (released July 13, 2026) confirms the cycle opened September 1, 2026 and closes November 19, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. EST, with awards starting between July 1 and September 30, 2027. It matters to the PI because there is no career-stage cap, NIH funding is not a prerequisite, and EHR, ctDNA/MRD and registry work fits squarely within NIH's definition of clinical research; it is disease-agnostic, so breast or ER+/HER2+ relevance carries no weight in review. The award is personal debt relief rather than research money, so it should be treated as a salary-support complement, not a project grant. The trap is the two hard gates: the PI must still carry educational debt of at least 20 percent of base salary at the time of award, and must be able to document, quarterly, a 50 percent research effort while holding clinical duties; a clinician with less than 50 percent protected research time cannot certify this. A further trap is the exclusion of anyone receiving research support or salary from a for-profit organization, which the PI should reconcile against industry consulting and industry-sponsored trial arrangements. Next step: confirm remaining debt balance and base salary, confirm protected research time is at least 50 percent, then register in the LRP portal, line up the mentor or institutional contact and the BCM business official certification, and submit before November 19, 2026.

grants.notes: The Beeson K76 is NIA's leadership-track career development award, co-funded with AFAR and the John A. Hartford Foundation, paying up to $225,000 in direct costs per year for up to five years at 8% F&A. It is the one NIH K designed for a clinician who already runs funded projects: candidates must have prior competitively awarded PD/PI support at the faculty level plus demonstrated leadership, while still holding ESI status. ESI status runs ten years from the end of clinical training, so a PI whose fellowship ended within the last ten years remains eligible for the 2026 and 2027 receipt dates, provided no R01-equivalent has been awarded. The genuine fit is a geriatric-oncology reframing of the computational angle, for example EHR or registry-based outcomes, ctDNA/MRD surveillance, or endocrine-therapy adherence in older women with ER+ breast cancer; NIA will not fund breast cancer science that merely happens to include older patients. The trap is effort: 75% protected time is mandatory, leaving 25% for clinic, which most breast medical oncologists cannot commit without an explicit institutional letter, and PAR-27-112 is the Clinical Trial Not Allowed version, so the investigator-initiated trial angle must sit outside the aims. The PI should confirm current funding history against the PD/PI requirement, secure an aging-focused co-mentor (BCM's Huffington Center on Aging or the DLDCCC geriatric oncology group), and check with NIA training staff whether November 12, 2026 (the NOFO date) or November 10 (the AFAR page) governs. A July 12, 2027 receipt date follows if the November cycle is too soon.

grants.notes: The Stephen I. Katz ESI R01 (PAR-25-322, reissue of PAR-24-075, open 2025-08-25 through 2028-08-26) is an uncapped, up-to-five-year NIH R01 reserved for Early Stage Investigators proposing a new research direction with no preliminary data; NCI is among the 24 participating ICs. It matters to the PI because the usual barrier to a first R01 for an MD-only clinician, the absence of a preliminary dataset, is inverted here: preliminary data are forbidden, and the review criteria instead ask for a sound premise and a credible justification of feasibility. A pivot into EHR/registry real-world-data methods or ctDNA/MRD analytics, or a biomarker-discovery project in HER2-heterogeneous or triple-positive disease, could be framed as a change in direction from a clinical-trials background, provided the PI has not already published in that exact area. The trap is twofold: any unpublished data in the application makes it noncompliant and withdrawn, and the one-page "New Research Direction" attachment is mandatory, so the PI must resist the reflex to show feasibility with a pilot analysis. The other gate is ESI standing, which runs ten years from the end of clinical training (fellowship 2019-2020, so roughly to 2029-2030) but is lost with any prior R01-equivalent award; the PI should confirm the ESI flag in the eRA Commons profile first. Clinical trials are not allowed under this NOFO, so the investigator-initiated-trial angle does not belong in this application. Standard cycles are late January, late May and late September for new applications; the 2026-09-28 date is too close to be realistic, so the PI should target 2027-01-26 (new) and contact the NCI program officer in the IC-specific table beforehand to confirm the project fits NCI's interest under this mechanism.

grants.notes: PAR-28-010 is the forecast reissue of the NIH Pragmatic Trials Collaboratory's embedded pragmatic and implementation trials NOFO, a phased milestone-driven cooperative agreement (planning phase then full trial) for large-scale trials run inside routine care across multiple health systems. The forecast was posted by NCCIH with an estimated NOFO date of 2026-11-24, an estimated application due date of 2027-02-23 and estimated awards 2027-12-01; no budget, award count or participating-IC list is given. For the PI the design fits the first two research angles well: an EHR-embedded, cluster- or registry-randomised trial (for example ctDNA-informed surveillance or endocrine-therapy adherence support) run across BCM, Harris Health and Houston Methodist is exactly the multi-system model the forecast asks for. grants.eligibility: Open to 'all responsible sources', including single entities or teams from private-sector, academic and nonprofit institutions; international institutions may apply if registered on SAM.gov before award. FDA states there are no specific educational or experience requirements for Principal Investigators, so an MD assistant professor with clinical duties is eligible as the technical lead on a BCM contract. The award is a research and development contract, not a grant, and BCM (not the PI) is the offeror. A Stage I package requires both a freestanding concept paper and a freestanding full proposal with cost proposal and statement of work; an optional early concept paper may be sent for feedback but is not a qualification step.
grants.notes: The FDA Broad Agency Announcement is the agency's annual, agency-wide contract solicitation for regulatory-science R&D; the Oncology Center of Excellence funds a slice of it and lists oncology real-world data/real-world evidence, clinical trial designs and endpoints/statistical methodology, precision oncology, oncology safety and patient-focused drug development among its FY26 interest areas. It matters to the PI because the first research angle maps directly onto what OCE says it wants: applied studies that solve a specific, practical problem encountered in the review of oncology products, such as calibrating EHR-derived external controls against trial arms or evaluating ctDNA/MRD as a regulatory endpoint in HER2-positive or ER-positive disease. There is no career-stage, degree or track restriction, clinical duties are not an issue, projects may run up to five years, and FY24 awards averaged about $1.0M (range $243K to $2.98M). The trap is treating it like a grant: it is a FAR contract submitted by BCM on SAM.gov with a full proposal, cost proposal and statement of work at Stage I, award rates run roughly 5 to 9 percent, and most losers are cut at high-level review for 'unaligned priorities' or 'lack of funds', so a proposal without a crisp regulatory question will not survive. The finder's list of proven awards is misleading: the ctDNA/MRD and RWE projects it cites were CERSI-funded, and the Minnesota breast-cancer project was an RFA award; only a few OCE projects on the active list are BAA-labelled. The FY26 Stage I cutoff (2026-02-24) has passed and the FY27 BAA is not yet posted; the pattern is a new BAA in December/January, optional early concept papers in early November, and a Stage I cutoff in late February. Next step: draft a three-page concept paper framed as a regulatory-science problem, email OCEScientificCollaborative@fda.hhs.gov for pre-submission interest, and loop in BCM's contracts office and SAM.gov registration before the FY27 BAA posts.

grants.program: Clinical Characterization of Cancer Therapy-induced Adverse Sequelae (R01) - PAR-25-145
grants.award_text: Budgets not capped but must reflect actual need; standard R01 up to 5 years (>$500K/yr direct costs would require prior NCI approval under NIH policy)
flags: scope-fit: toxicity/sequelae is adjacent to, not inside, the PI's four angles
non-responsive trap: acute/reversible sequelae and resistance studies excluded
prioritises mechanism-plus-phenotype; pure RWD/EHR descriptive study is weak
finder URL (Grants.gov 357015) did not render; NIH Guide PAR-25-145 page used as primary
grants.eligibility: Any PD/PI with the skills, knowledge and resources to carry out the research; no career-stage, degree or track restriction, and an assistant professor with clinical duties can lead. Clinical trial optional. Projects must clinically characterize persistent or delayed therapy-induced sequelae and couple that phenotyping with mechanistic understanding; collaborations between clinical and basic-science investigators are encouraged and mechanism-plus-phenotype projects are prioritized. Studies of acute, reversible, non-progressive sequelae, of treatment resistance, of non-FDA-approved agents in preclinical models, or of symptomatic events in non-cancer conditions are non-responsive.
grants.notes: NCI R01 PAR (clinical trial optional) for research that identifies mechanisms of persistent or delayed cancer-therapy-induced adverse sequelae, clinically characterizes them with longitudinal phenotyping, and translates that into interventions; listed examples include cardiovascular toxicity, pulmonary fibrosis, neuropathy, neurocognitive impairment, lymphedema, fatigue and immune-related events. Standard NIH R01 dates run through October 5, 2027 (next new-application date October 5, 2026; resubmission November 5, 2026), budgets uncapped, up to 5 years, and any PD/PI may apply, so the PI's rank, degree and clinical duties pose no barrier. It matters to this profile as a side door for the ADC/HER2 and endocrine-therapy work: longitudinal EHR-plus-biomarker characterization of chronic anti-HER2 cardiotoxicity, ADC-related lung injury that persists or progresses, or long-term endocrine-therapy sequelae in ER+/HER2+ patients, paired with a mechanistic co-investigator from the Smith Breast Center. The trap is the non-responsive list: acute, reversible, non-progressive sequelae are excluded, which rules out most short-course ADC ILD and reversible trastuzumab LVEF drops unless the aims are framed around persistent or delayed injury; resistance studies are also excluded, so endocrine-resistance aims cannot ride along. Reviewers will prioritise projects coupling mechanism with clinical phenotype, so a purely descriptive registry or EHR study is unlikely to score. Next step: decide whether a chronic-toxicity aim genuinely exists in the PI's cohort data, recruit a basic-science co-PI with a mechanistic model of that sequela, and target the February 5, 2027 date if October 2026 is too soon. Use the NIH Guide page, not the Grants.gov synopsis, as the record URL.
grants.evidence: NIH Guide PAR-25-145 (fetched 2026-09-10): Application Due Dates table lists new-application dates 'October 05, 2026', 'February 05, 2027', 'June 05, 2027', 'October 05, 2027' with resubmission dates one month later; 'Expiration Date January 8, 2028' (establishes active status and next deadline 2026-10-05). 'Application budgets are not limited but need to reflect the actual needs of the proposed project'; maximum project period 5 years (award). 'Any individual(s) with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to carry out the proposed research' may serve as PD/PI (no career cap or track gate). Clinical trial 'Optional: Accepting applications that either propose or do not propose clinical trial(s).' Scope: 'identify the mechanisms of therapy-induced adverse sequelae, clinically characterize the adverse sequelae, and translate the mechanistic understanding into therapeutic approaches'; 'Collaborations between clinical and basic science investigators are encouraged, and projects that couple the mechanistic knowledge with clinical phenotype will be prioritized.' Non-responsive: 'Studies focused on acute, reversible, and non-progressive adverse sequelae; Exploring resistance to cancer treatment; Using Pre-clinical models to determine adverse events of non-FDA approved anti-cancer agents; and Exploring the development of symptomatic adverse events in non-cancer conditions.'

grants.eligibility: Standard NIH applicant organizations (higher education, nonprofits, for-profits, governments, tribal entities, foreign institutions); no career-stage or track restriction. The trial must meet the NIH clinical-trial definition and be relevant to the research mission of the participating ICs, which in this forecast are exclusively NHLBI programs (cardiovascular, lung, blood, sleep, and translation/implementation science CFDAs; contact is the NHLBI Division of Cardiovascular Sciences). The application must present the scientific and operational plan for the trial plus a comprehensive plan for coordination, data management, and biostatistics. grants.notes: PAR-27-125 is a grants.gov forecast (posted 2026-07-01) for a reissue of NHLBI's multi-site investigator-initiated clinical trial UG3/UH3 cooperative agreement, not a trans-NIH vehicle with ICs still to be named. Every assistance listing attached to the record is an NHLBI program and the agency contact is the NHLBI Division of Cardiovascular Sciences, so trials must be relevant to heart, lung, blood, or sleep research. A ctDNA/MRD-guided or de-escalation trial in ER+/HER2+ breast cancer would not be responsive; NCI does not participate, and NCI's own multi-site IIT routes (cooperative groups, NCTN, R01/U01 clinical-trial-required PARs) are the correct vehicles for that idea. The trap is treating the "participating ICs" language as an invitation for oncology trials; it is boilerplate carried over from NHLBI's own PAR series. The only conceivable fit for the PI is as a co-investigator on a cardio-oncology trial (for example HER2-directed therapy cardiotoxicity), which is outside the four stated angles. The grants.gov estimates are NOFO posting around 2026-11-16, applications around 2027-02-16, and awards around 2027-10-01, but none is a posted deadline. Recommended action is to retire this candidate and, if a multi-site IIT vehicle is needed, look to NCI mechanisms instead.

grants.career_cap: Initial faculty appointment within the last 7 years at submission; NIH ESI-equivalent (no R01/P01/U01 or equivalent at application)
grants.eligibility: Junior faculty (Instructor, Assistant or Associate Professor, and similar post-fellowship ranks) holding an MD, DO, PhD or equivalent who received their initial faculty appointment within the last 7 years at a US research institution as of the submission date, and who meet NIH Early Stage Investigator criteria (no R01, P01, U01 or equivalent at application; NIH LRP participants excluded). Applicants need a research mentor, institutional support documenting 30% of professional time for research in general, and US citizenship, permanent residency or a visa valid for the 2-year award. Research on Gilead products and interventional studies administering any pharmaceutical drug are excluded; co-PIs are not funded; funding may not duplicate other current or pending support. Exceptions to the 7-year window are considered for parental leave, bereavement or military service.
grants.notes: The Gilead Research Scholars Program in Solid Tumors (US) is an industry-funded, independently reviewed junior-faculty award; the 2026 cycle is explicitly limited to breast, endometrial, ovarian or small cell lung cancer and funds a minimum of three scholars at up to $180,000 over two years, paid to the institution. It matters to the PI because the scientific-focus list names disparities, resistance mechanisms, biomarkers, genomic predictors of response and PRO/QoL work, which map onto the PI's real-world data, ER+/HER2+ biomarker and equity angles, and because the 30% research-time requirement is framed against patient-care duties, so a clinician applicant is expected. The award is only for NIH-style early-stage investigators: no R01/P01/U01 at application and an initial faculty appointment within the last seven years as of 13 November 2026, which puts a 2020 appointment inside the window and a 2019 appointment outside it unless parental-leave or similar exceptions apply, so the PI should confirm the exact appointment date before drafting. Two traps: any project touching a Gilead product (notably sacituzumab govitecan for the ADC angle) is diverted to Gilead's separate ESR portal and is ineligible here, and interventional trials that administer a drug are excluded, so the investigator-initiated trial angle cannot be the proposal. Round 1 requires only a one-page specific aims document by 13 November 2026; invited applicants submit a five-page proposal by 10 March 2027 with notifications in February and May 2027. Next step: check the appointment date and R01 status, identify a mentor, and draft a non-interventional aims page (ctDNA/MRD registry, EHR cohort or disparities work in HER2-positive or triple-positive disease) with a budget that keeps indirects at or below 10%.

grants.notes: The GC-CPEH Pilot Project Program is the seed mechanism of the NIEHS P30 Gulf Coast Center for Precision Environmental Health, a joint BCM/UTMB/UTHealth centre, offering up to $40,000 direct costs for one year (no F&A, no extensions) to faculty at Instructor level and above; GC-CPEH membership is not required for the Full Pilot track. The fit is indirect: the RFA welcomes big data, bioinformatics, epidemiology, and community research, so a real-world-data or catchment-area project could qualify only if it is genuinely about environmental or place-based exposures (for example, residential exposure history linked to breast cancer outcomes or endocrine-disrupting exposure and endocrine resistance), not breast oncology with an environmental veneer. Funded projects to date centre on toxicology, exposure science, and environmental justice; none listed mentions breast cancer. The next step is to watch for the Round 9 RFA, historically posted around March with a May LOI, and to identify a GC-CPEH member (data-science or exposure-science) co-investigator so the proposal uses a Facility Core, which the Center also prioritizes. The Rapid Response track ($20,000, rolling) is closed to the PI unless GC-CPEH membership is obtained first.
